headline: Week Ahead: BOJ and Fed may Pay Heavy Price if They Disappoint the Market
summary: Marc Chandler's week-ahead analysis says markets are strongly priced for a 25bp BOJ hike and about an 87% probability of a Fed hike. With US yields already high and oil-driven inflation pressure elevated, disappointment by either central bank could produce an outsized cross-asset reaction.

US2Y.source: U.S. Treasury daily par yield via Treasury Rate Watch

US10Y.source: U.S. Treasury daily par yield via Treasury Rate Watch

learning_profile.effect: Favored MIXED 4/10 over weak low-confidence directional calls because leakage-safe ACTIONABLE segments show materially stronger performance for neutral setups, while low-confidence directional segments are REDUCE_OR_AVOID/KEEP_NEUTRAL.

predictions.mechanism: A BOJ hike is heavily priced and a hawkish signal is expected, but the yen reaction is uncertain and stronger yen pressure can weigh on exporters while policy credibility can support broader sentiment.
predictions.invalidation: A clear BOJ surprise versus pricing that drives a sustained one-way yen move and broad Japanese equity repricing.

predictions.mechanism: Fed hike odds near 87% and US10Y near 5% create valuation pressure, while failure to hike could initially lower front-end yields but damage inflation credibility and steepen the curve.
predictions.invalidation: A decisive Fed repricing that sends Treasury yields sustainably lower with stable inflation expectations, or sharply higher with broad risk-off confirmation.

predictions.mechanism: High yields and oil-driven inflation remain headwinds, but Friday's oil pullback and easing VIX offset part of the pressure ahead of the binary Fed decision.
predictions.invalidation: A sustained synchronized move in oil, yields and equity breadth that resolves the current conflicting macro signals.

predictions.mechanism: A Fed surprise can move cyclicals through both growth expectations and financing costs; current oil and yield signals remain conflicting.
predictions.invalidation: Clear one-way repricing of Fed policy accompanied by confirming moves in yields, dollar and equity breadth.

predictions.mechanism: Gold faces opposing forces from elevated geopolitical risk and policy uncertainty versus a firm dollar and very high real/nominal Treasury yields.
predictions.invalidation: A decisive break in DXY and Treasury yields in the same direction that removes the current macro conflict.
